title: Speeding up a clip in an edit leaves no black hole and keeps the transition after it
goal: Setting a clip to play faster shortens it, and today that leaves a stretch of black where the clip used to be and silently removes the transition on the cut after it. Changing a clip's speed should keep the edit joined up, the way Premiere's rate stretch does with ripple, or at least never leave a black gap without saying so.
notes:
User, 2026-11-26: "I tried making one this morning. it was boring, the transitions were a bit buggy (e.g. 3d transitions wouldn't fade in and would immediately cover content, text would be clipped in weird spots, the transitions were dull). I don't see anything queued or done with improving the features and quality to make amazing sizzle reels (with a bunch of music presets that can create epic build ups and intensity and draw emotion)." 

Found making a reel through the MCP tools: clip E478 at 14 to 17 s set to 200 percent became 14 to 15.5 s; 15.5 to 17 black; the doorway at 17 s disappeared from read_document's cuts. Not the speed ramp work (motion-that-feels-like-apple-springs-speed-ramps), which is about easing between speeds.
acceptance: Reproduced first at Next defaults: a run of clips with transitions on each cut, set the middle clip to 200 percent (Clip > Speed, and run_command set_speed): today the clip ends 1.5 s early, the frames until the next clip are black (only overlay text shows), and the transition on the following cut is gone (queue/audits/2026-11-26-sizzle-intake/speed-200-leaves-black-gap.png).

Decide and write in the audit what speed does to the clips after it, against Premiere and Final Cut (ripple by default on a primary storyline is the usual answer); the transition on the next cut survives in every case, and when a gap is left on purpose it is visible on the timeline and named in the answer to the agent.
Slower speeds (50, 25) push later clips along the same way rather than covering them. Undo puts everything back in one step.

Unit tests in PhotonzCore that fail on today's code for the gap and for the lost transition, plus a walk. Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.

log.note: Re-checked on Photonz Dev 0.25.0 (today's main) on 2026-11-26: the first reel ran on the user's 0.23.0 app. Still reproduces, same numbers: see queue/audits/2026-11-26-sizzle-intake/on-0.25-dev/ and the README's Correction section.

Reproduced in PhotonzCore first: SpeedRippleTests, three clips A 0-4s, B 4-7s, C 7-10s with dissolves on both cuts; on today's code B at 200% left C at 7-10s (black 5.5-7s) and editPoints read [4000] only, so the B>C dissolve was not drawn (still stored on C, just no longer meeting); 50% and 25% left C under B. 7 of 8 tests failed before the fix.

Chose rippling the clip's own track (plus captions heard off it, sparing locked layers) over every track, because it matches Final Cut's primary storyline, Premiere's Speed/Duration with Ripple Edit, and the freeze default 'This track' (user, 2026-10-17); music on another track is not broken up by a retime. Fix: PhotonzDocument.setClipSpeed -> rippleOwnTrack (ClipPieces.swift); setSectionSpeed now retimes latest clip first so a ripple never moves a later clip out from under the range. No gap is ever left, so nothing needs naming to the agent; set_speed's option text now says the clips after it move.

Verified: SpeedRippleTests 8/8 (faster, 50 and 25, back to 100, a gap kept, other tracks stay, one undo, piece of a cut clip, section across a cut); Scripts/test.sh exit 0; new walk speeding-up-a-clip-keeps-the-edit-joined-walk green at Next defaults with 3 real captures (looked at 1-double and 2-half: edit point at 0:03 and 0:14 with Cross dissolve on it); speed walks a-retimed-clip, command-r, cut-on-the-timeline, half-speed-reads-alike, speed-stops-ramp, speed-a-stretch, the-speed-curve all green. video-panel-order-walk fails at step 11 on panel section order, before any speed step, already owned by walks-that-fail-in-the-full-sweep-28.

left rough: speed stop edits on a ramp (SpeedStops.swift: setSpeedStop, moveSpeedStop, freezeSpeedStop...) go through editClip and do not ripple, so they probably leave the same gap; not reproduced here, so not filed; noted on motion-that-feels-like-apple-springs-speed-ramps. Also left rough: a title on another track over a later clip stays put and can end up over a different shot (no connected clips in Photonz).

Clip > Speed and set_speed now move the clips after the retimed clip on its own track by however much it grew or shrank (PhotonzDocument.setClipSpeed -> rippleOwnTrack), so 200% leaves no black and the next cut keeps its transition, 50/25% push along, one undo. Verified by SpeedRippleTests (failed before), full test.sh green, new walk speeding-up-a-clip-keeps-the-edit-joined-walk green at Next defaults with real captures; audit queue/audits/2026-11-26-speed-ripple.json.
